_websearch_sources.run_instructions: ROTATED as of 2026-08-23; do not go back to 'run every active daily source'. Run `.venv/bin/python pipeline/websearch_rotation.py` at Step 1c: it prints the `rotation_per_run` daily sources with the oldest `last_run` (nulls first) plus their queries, flags anything that has gone more than 7 days without running, and reports which monthly sources are due. After running them, record ONLY the ones that actually ran with `--mark "<name>" ...`. Marking a source you skipped is the single way this mechanism can silently lose coverage. Monthly sources are gated by calendar month and never consume a rotation slot. Use `--all` for an interactive full sweep.
_websearch_sources.rotation_rationale: Step 1c used to demand all 16 active daily sources every run, and the way that lost was by being skipped outright: 2026-08-21 ran zero of them, 2026-08-23 ran four. Measured over the 11 runs carrying channel_stats (2026-08-10 onward), WebSearch discovery produced 46 new companies and 13 enrollments across 121 source-runs, about 9 source-runs per company enrolled, against 21 enrollments for the LinkedIn harvest at one Gmail call per run. The channel works; the marginal source is expensive. At 6/run every source is hit roughly every 3 days for ~40% of the cost, and a 3-day gap is nearly free because these sources discover companies rather than perishable reqs. Caveat worth keeping honest: n=11 runs, and the low-source days were also thin days generally, so the yield figure is directional, not settled. Revisit once weekly_channel_report.py has more windows; some of these sources may deserve disabling rather than rotating.
_websearch_sources.rotation_seeded_note: Date the rotation state was introduced. websearch_rotation.py uses it to suppress the never-run staleness alarm until the first full cycle has had time to complete (ceil(sources/rotation_per_run) + 1 days); on a freshly seeded config every source is null, so the alarm would fire on all of them and carry no information. After that window a null last_run really does mean a source is falling through. Do not update this field on later runs.

_blind_spot_companies.description: Named-company rotation for the pipeline's hardest structural gap: companies with NO pollable ATS. The poller speaks Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever, Workday, SmartRecruiters and Workable; these companies use custom career sites (Google, Apple, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Delta) or a Workday tenant whose real site name has not been resolved yet. They cannot be enrolled, so the ONLY way they ever surface is a targeted search. Added 2026-07-27 after a user-surfaced Atlanta alert turned up a Google role (Product Solutions Manager, Home) that was a genuinely strong fit and was invisible to every automated source. Verified the same day that Google's careers site has no public JSON API (two candidate endpoints both 404).

_comeet_notes: ats='comeet'. Comeet has no slug-style identifier: the API needs a per-company `comeet_uid` (e.g. 'F6.007') and a public widget `comeet_token`, both embedded in the company's own careers page source (grep the page for 'uid' and 'token') -- scrape them once at enrollment and store on the watchlist entry; validate_config.py enforces both, same pattern as workday's wd_* fields. `slug` is still required as a human-readable identifier for dedup keys (use the company name, e.g. 'stampli'). Added 2026-08-20 after Stampli -- rejected as unpollable on 2026-08-04 -- turned out to have this API live the whole time: third instance of the unsupported-ATS-looks-like-no-ATS miss class (Napier AI/Pinpoint, Nerdio/Rippling, both fixed 2026-08-12). API verified live 2026-08-20. Known limits: no posting-creation date (only time_updated -- used as a freshness approximation, can overstate freshness on recently-touched old reqs); no salary data (always neutral); `details=true` returns Description/Requirements HTML (flattened into `description` for the industry exclusion); internal-only postings carry is_internal=true and are dropped by fetch_comeet. DISCOVERY CLOSED 2026-09-03 (Upwind Security, the FOURTH instance and the sharpest, because Comeet was already supported by the poller -- only discovery was broken). harvest_ats.py could never resolve a Comeet company: it generates name-derived SLUGS, and Comeet has no slug, so Upwind was rejected 2026-09-02 as 'no board resolved from deterministic name-variant slugs' while running a live 58-position board whose 'Technical Account Manager (US Remote)' req the LinkedIn harvest had surfaced twice. probe_comeet() inverts the walk for this ATS only -- name -> guessed own domain -> careers page -> scraped comeet_uid/comeet_token -> board -- and runs after the cheap slug probes and before Workday. The scraped page URL is stored as comeet_careers_url on the entry so a wrong domain guess is auditable; nothing reads it. Both companies confirmed on Comeet (Stampli, Upwind) use the Comeet WordPress plugin, which emits the credentials inline in a `var comeetvar = {...}` block, so a plain GET finds them; the generic script embed (credentials in a comeet.co careers-api URL) and a bounded same-origin script-follow are also handled but are so far untested against a real site. Watch for false positives from a company HOMEPAGE: sitewide Comeet script/CSS includes trip the markup check while carrying no credentials, which is why any careers path that redirects to the site root is treated as a soft 404.
_jazzhr_notes: ats='jazzhr'. slug is the tenant subdomain of applytojob.com (e.g. 'rethink' from rethink.applytojob.com/apply/) -- read it off the company's own careers page, because it is often NOT derivable from the company name (RethinkFirst -> 'rethink'), so slug_variants() alone may never find it. Scraped, not an API (JazzHR's JSON API needs a per-employer key): the board page is server-rendered HTML, one list-group-item per posting carrying title, location and department. No salary and no posting date exist anywhere on it, so both are always neutral and MAX_POSTING_AGE_DAYS never filters these boards. JazzHR NEVER 404s a bad slug -- a dead slug either 302s to www.jazzhr.com/job-seekers or serves a fixed 'JazzHR - Inactive Career Page' with HTTP 200 -- so jazzhr_board_live() checks the final host AND the page title before trusting a response; without both checks a name-variant sweep enrols amazon/microsoft/oracle. Added 2026-09-03 after RethinkFirst was rejected as unpollable twice (an ATS-coverage gap reported as a slug gap, same class as Pinpoint 08-12 and Paylocity 08-28); PayMitto enrolled the same day. harvest_ats.py probes it among the cheap ATSes, reusing the poller's parser so the probe and the daily fetch cannot drift.
_pinpoint_notes: ats='pinpoint'. slug is the company's Pinpoint subdomain (e.g. 'napier' from napier.pinpointhq.com) -- find it from the company's careers-page URL. Public JSON API, no auth, no pagination wrapper observed (returns the full board in one `data` array). Added 2026-08-12 after Napier AI was user-surfaced (LinkedIn alert) and turned out to have a clean public API the whole time -- this was a pure discovery gap, not a structural one. No posting-date field is exposed by this endpoint, so freshness is always neutral for Pinpoint hits (same 'no data -> don't filter' treatment as Workday). Salary only appears when `compensation_visible` is true.
_paylocity_notes: ats='paylocity'. UNLIKE EVERY OTHER ATS HERE, `slug` is a GUID, not a name-derived string -- it is the identifier in the careers URL /Recruiting/Jobs/All/<GUID>. Nothing derives it from a company name, so harvest_ats.py can NEVER auto-resolve a Paylocity board; these must be enrolled by hand from a careers-page URL. Two host forms, both verified live 2026-08-28: the shared `recruiting.paylocity.com` (Paylocity's CUSTOMERS, the common case) and a tenant-prefixed `<id>recruiting.paylocity.com` (Paylocity itself is 2000). Set `paylocity_host` only for the prefixed form; it defaults to the shared host. This is a MULTI-TENANT platform, so the adapter is worth more than the one company that prompted it: five distinct tenants were confirmed parsing identically (229/94/24/17/3 jobs). No JSON API exists -- the listing page server-renders the complete job array into the HTML under a `"Jobs":[...]` key, so a plain GET works and no headless browser is needed; fetch_paylocity extracts it by bracket-balancing rather than regex, because Description strings contain braces and quotes. A bogus GUID returns HTTP 200 with no Jobs array and is reported as an error rather than treated as an empty board. IsRemote IS DELIBERATELY IGNORED in favour of LocationName: on Paylocity's own board the two disagree in BOTH directions (33 city-named jobs flagged IsRemote=true because they are home-based field-sales territories, and 13 'Remote, US' jobs flagged IsRemote=false), the same trap as Ashby's isRemote corrected the same day. PublishedDate is a real ISO timestamp, so freshness works normally here, unlike Pinpoint and Rippling. Salary is NOT in the listing payload; it appears only on the per-job detail page at /Recruiting/Jobs/Details/<JobId>, so salary is always neutral for Paylocity hits. Added 2026-08-28 after Paylocity was twice rejected as unpollable -- an ATS-coverage gap, not a slug or scoring gap.
_rippling_notes: ats='rippling'. slug is the path segment after ats.rippling.com/ (e.g. 'nerdio-careers' from ats.rippling.com/nerdio-careers/jobs) -- find it from the company's careers-page URL. The page LOOKS JS-rendered (Next.js) but is actually server-side rendered: a plain GET with a browser User-Agent returns full HTML containing a `__NEXT_DATA__` script tag with the job list pre-embedded as a dehydrated TanStack Query cache (`props.pageProps.dehydratedState.queries[0].state.data.items`), so no headless browser is needed. Added 2026-08-12 after Nerdio was user-surfaced (LinkedIn/Indeed alert); confirmed a naive `requests.get` without a User-Agent can trip Cloudflare, so fetch_rippling always sends one. Paginated at pageSize=20 server-side; fetch_rippling requests additional pages via `?page=N` up to a cap, mirroring fetch_smartrecruiters' pagination-cap pattern -- unverified against a board with more than one page as of the 2026-08-12 add, so treat multi-page Rippling boards as lower-confidence until one is seen live. No posting-date or salary field is exposed in the list view (only on each job's own detail page, not fetched), so both are always neutral for Rippling hits.
_smartrecruiters_notes: ats='smartrecruiters'. slug is the case-sensitive company identifier (e.g. 'BoschGroup', not 'bosch') — find it from a careers.smartrecruiters.com/{slug} or jobs.smartrecruiters.com/{slug} URL. Public postings API, no auth. Added 2026-06-30 to widen enrollable boards beyond GH/Ashby/Lever/Workday. FIXED 2026-08-06: fetch_smartrecruiters was single-page (limit=100), which silently hid postings past position 100 on large boards -- caught the hard way when a live, 6-day-old, Atlanta-based 'Manager, Customer Success Management' role at ServiceNow (416+ total postings) never appeared anywhere in poller output, only surfacing via a LinkedIn alert Aneesh spotted by hand. Now paginates up to SMARTRECRUITERS_MAX_POSTINGS (500). Note: offset-based pagination against a live-mutating board isn't perfectly race-safe -- a posting can still theoretically shift across a page boundary mid-fetch -- but this closes the vast majority of the gap (100 -> ~465 postings scanned for ServiceNow). DISCOVERY CLOSED 2026-09-03, same miss class as _comeet_notes and the same day: poll_ats.py had read this ATS since 2026-06-30 while harvest_ats.py never probed it, so a SmartRecruiters-hosted company was rejected as unpollable=True -- the one flag that stops it being re-checked. Unlike Comeet this needed no new resolution model, since these boards ARE slug-addressed and slug_variants() has generated the capitalised forms since 2026-08-27. The one non-obvious requirement: the postings API returns 200 with totalFound:0 for a nonexistent slug instead of 404ing, so probe() must treat an empty result as NO BOARD (return None) and never as a resolved-but-empty one -- an empty list routes into _confirm_empty, whose re-probe gets the same confident 200 and would confirm a slug collision rather than catch it, which is exactly how a 2026-08-28 sweep reported ten resolved companies that were all collisions. It also probes LAST among the cheap ATSes for that reason: it cannot 404 a bad slug, so a genuine Greenhouse/Ashby board should get to answer first. Verified 2026-09-03 against Nexthink (slug 'nexthink', 100 jobs) and Bosch Group ('boschgroup', 100 jobs) -- note both resolved LOWERCASE, so the API is case-insensitive on the slug even though the canonical identifier is cased; the concatenation is what matters ('boschgroup', never 'bosch'). Not added to prune(), which distinguishes dead-404 from resolved-empty and would report every quiet SmartRecruiters board as dead.

_scoring_config.notes_near_miss: Near-misses are listed (with links) in the email digest but NOT tailored, so Aneesh can eyeball them. Two kinds, unioned: (A) score near-miss — passes all hard filters incl. salary, but scores below light_tailoring_threshold (no lower score bound, capture all). (B) salary near-miss — passes all other filters but salary midpoint is below salary_floor_usd yet at or above near_miss_salary_floor_usd. See SKILL Step 2 + Step 5.
_scoring_config.notes_cap_pending_age: Added 2026-07-27. An applied entry with outcome=null stops counting toward the company cap after this many days. Rationale: outcome=null was doing double duty -- it means both 'still waiting to hear' and 'nobody ever recorded a result' -- so a silent application blocked its company forever. An audit found EVERY capped company was frozen by applications 41 or 81 days old with zero recorded outcomes (Samsara 7 at 81d, Anthropic 5 at 81d, Observe.AI and Hightouch 3 each at 81d, Glean 4 spanning 41-81d). After 60 days of silence an application is realistically a rejection, not in flight. At this value Samsara/Anthropic/Observe.AI/Hightouch/Glean all unblock and Talkdesk (3 at 41d) correctly stays capped. This is a WORKAROUND for the missing outcome-confirmation loop, not a substitute: once application confirmations actually flow in (see daily_task_prompt.md Step 0.5), real outcomes will retire these entries properly and this age-out becomes a backstop rather than the primary mechanism.
_scoring_config.notes_salary: Compare the MIDPOINT of a listed base-salary range against salary_floor_usd — never the bottom or top. Single figure: use as-is. OTE-only: estimate base (80% for variable/sales roles, 100% otherwise). No salary listed: do not filter, treat as neutral in scoring. See SKILL Step 2b for the authoritative rule.
_scoring_config.notes_freshness: Add +10 for postings ≤2 days old, +2 for ≤7 days. Validated by empirical data: response rates fall sharply after 48 hours.
_scoring_config.notes_small_company: Counterweight for the sub-500 segment, which the watchlist + AI/Atlanta bonuses structurally bury (those bonuses correlate with big, well-known companies). Add +15 if the company's headcount_band is ≤50-200, +8 if 201-500, 0 above. Applies ONLY when the company entry carries a headcount_band field; if absent, treat as neutral (0) — do NOT guess. This is a COMPANY-LEVEL bonus and counts toward the +30 company-bonus cap in CLAUDE.md alongside AI/ML, watchlist, Atlanta, IoT. Consequence by design: a small AI-native company (AI +20 + small +15 = 35 → clamped to 30) gains little since it already surfaces; the lift lands where it's needed — small NON-AI companies (vertical SaaS, dev infra) like PermitFlow/Antithesis/Mintlify that have real role fit but no AI/Atlanta bonus to clear threshold. Rationale: at a 150-person company a support-ops/CSM/implementation hire has real scope; at a 3,000-person company it's one of dozens.
_scoring_config.notes: Light tailoring for IC-level roles 78-87. Full tailoring for 88+. Skip below 78. Capped companies require 110+ regardless of tier. Cap rule: count entries where applied=true AND outcome=null (pending applications). If that count ≥ company_cap_max_applied_pending, new roles need company_cap_threshold to surface. Queued/unapplied roles do NOT count toward the cap — only submitted applications do.

function_mismatch_titles._narrow_admin_rule_2026_08_28: THE DURABLE PRINCIPLE, confirmed by Aneesh in his own words on 2026-08-28: 'it's the narrow admin work I don't want.' Use this to judge titles this list has not seen yet, because the patterns below are only the instances observed so far. The line is ALTITUDE, not domain: he wants to OWN a function (build the tooling, run the adoption program, decide what the system should do) and does not want to BE someone's platform administrator (configure the tool, take the tickets, hold the certification). CRM Administrator and Applications Administrator were added in this pass because the first cut keyed on the GTM qualifier and missed them, and they are narrow admin by his stated test even though no GTM word appears. The two readings converge rather than compete: GTM systems roles at these companies ARE administration in manager clothing, which is visible in the Baseten JD's own responsibilities ('Own adminship, configuration, and enablement for Pylon, Gong, Sales Navigator, Outreach, and Prospect', 'Co-own Salesforce'). What survives at +22 is the function-ownership half of tier2c: Business Systems MANAGER, Support Systems Manager, Internal Tools Manager, Tooling Manager, Automation Manager, Platform Operations Manager, and the Applications MANAGER family. Analyst-level is deliberately NOT demoted: he applied to Wiz's 'Sr. Business Systems Analyst' (106) unprompted, so the analyst rung is acceptable to him where the administrator rung is not.
function_mismatch_titles._gtm_systems_demotion_2026_08_28: The six patterns after 'Corporate Development' demote the GTM-QUALIFIED and SALESFORCE-ADMIN-TITLED half of tier2c. They are NOT removed from tier2c: leaving them there keeps them matching and surfacing as digest FYI lines, which is the whole point of this section. Evidence, from a review Aneesh prompted on 2026-08-28 after reading the Baseten GTM Systems Manager JD and saying it looked very different from what he does: every GTM-qualified or Salesforce-admin-titled systems role the pipeline has ever surfaced has gone unsent, and every systems role he DID send lacked that qualifier. Unsent (0 of 5): Zscaler 'Senior Business Systems Analyst-GTM' (88), Salesloft 'Salesforce Business Systems Administrator' (101), CrowdStrike 'Sr. Business Systems Analyst, Go-to-Market' (116, the second-highest score in the whole tracker), Abnormal AI 'Senior Salesforce Administrator, GTM Systems' (109), Baseten 'GTM Systems Manager' (102). Sent (3 of 3): Outreach 'Manager, Customer Operations (Revenue Operations)' (122, tier1 title), Outreach 'Senior GTM AI Advisor' (98, AI advisory), Wiz 'Sr. Business Systems Analyst' (106, unqualified). Four of those five unsent roles got FULL tailoring WITH a cover letter, so this was costing the run's single most expensive artifact roughly once a week. Note the discriminator is NOT the hard-requirement cap: Wiz was capped to light tier and he applied anyway, while CrowdStrike carried cap_trigger 'none' at priority tier and he did not. The tier2c 'notes' field assumed the salary floor would screen the Salesforce-admin end of this family out on its own; that assumption fails at AI-native companies, which pay $160K-$200K for the same work.
function_mismatch_titles._gtm_systems_demotion_verification: Deliberately narrow. A bare 'GTM' pattern would be the obvious catch-all and is NOT used, because it would also demote Outreach's 'Senior GTM AI Advisor', a role Aneesh actually applied to. Verified against the real TitleMatcher on 2026-08-28 over all eight historical titles plus seven controls: 5 of 5 unsent roles demote, 0 of 3 sent roles demote, 0 of 7 controls demote (Business Systems Manager, Support Systems Manager, Internal Tools Manager, Automation Manager, Enterprise Applications Manager, Revenue Operations Manager, and tier1 Technical Support Operations Manager all survive). Zscaler's 'Senior Business Systems Analyst-GTM' was expected to slip through as a bare '-GTM' suffix and does NOT: tokenize() splits the hyphen, so 'GTM' and 'Systems' both appear as tokens and _tokens_near matches the 'GTM Systems' pattern. That also means the patterns are token-subset matches rather than substrings, so word order and punctuation do not matter. Reverting is a one-line delete per pattern; per this section's own rule, a variant that ever looks like a REAL fit should be moved back to a scoring tier rather than tailored out of the function_mismatch section.
function_mismatch_titles._known_issue_2026_07_27: The protected_tiers mechanism checks only the title's BEST tier match, not every tier it matches. 'Product Customer Success Manager' is documented below as staying live via tier4 protection, but it actually resolves to tier3 (score 15 beats tier4's 8), and tier3 is not protected -- so it IS demoted today, contrary to the note. Pre-existing, not caused by the 2026-07-27 product-ops carve-out (it contains no contiguous 'product manager' and matches none of the new tier2 entries). Proper fix is for is_function_mismatch to honor ANY protected tier the title matches rather than just the best-scoring one; deferred as low value since tier4 is the weakest stretch tier.

Protected tiers override the demotion: a title whose best tier match is tier1/tier2/tier4 is never demoted, so 'Product Engagement Manager, User Operations' (tier1, contains 'Product…Manager'), 'Support Engineering Manager' (tier1, contains 'Engineering Manager'), and 'Product Customer Success Manager' (tier4, contains 'Product…Manager') stay live. tier3/supplemental/tier2b/borderline matches get checked. 'Product Manager', 'Technical Program Manager', and 'Sales Engineer' were moved here FROM supplemental_exact_titles, where their 'surface for review' intent had turned into daily shortlist crowding. If one of these classes ever produces a real fit, move that specific title variant to a scoring tier.
